newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint ends firmer vs dlr, low BCE futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Forint ends firmer vs dlr, low BCE futures trade.

text.p: The Hungarian forint closed firmer on Thursday as the U.S. unit eased from its two-year high against the mark on European markets, dealers said.

The forint ended at 163.48/53 to the dollar, compared to an opening level of 162.68/73, but stayed close to the national bank resistance level (bid) as international movements remained the only determining factor.
The bid stood at 163.40 at the close.
"The domestic market remained quiet while we watched developments in the dollar/mark," said Szilvia Kucsera of Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank.

The forint floats against a basket of currencies made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark, making changes in its level against the dollar inversely proportional to movements in the dollar/mark cross.
Turnover on the currency futures market of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) was low, at 2.98 billion forints.
A new contract in the Swiss franc for December 1997 -- opening at 139.20 forints -- made up half of total trade.
